$mediumNotes.whatWorks: medium.com/feed/tag/<tag> returns valid RSS. medium.com/feed/<publication> failed at the connection level (curl exit, no HTTP status) for netflix-techblog, pinterest-engineering, zomato-technology and walmartglobaltech — so use each publication's CUSTOM DOMAIN instead (netflixtechblog.com/feed, itnext.io/feed, levelup.gitconnected.com/feed, blog.bytebytego.com/feed).
$mediumNotes.noiseWarning: Medium tag feeds and the large programming publications carry a lot of beginner listicles and AI-generated filler. They are included for breadth, but the genuinely high-signal senior-engineer content in this project comes from the individual blogs filed under `architecture` (Marc Brooker, Dan Luu, Julia Evans) and from InfoQ, ByteByteGo and The Pragmatic Engineer — not from tag feeds.
$mediumNotes.paywall: Member-only Medium stories are truncated in RSS, so the summary is a teaser and the link may hit the metered paywall.
$mediumNotes.ciRisk: Medium does connection-level blocking from some networks. Expect these feeds to be less reliable from GitHub Actions runners than from a laptop.
$mediumNotes.alsoTested: highscalability.com/rss.xml returns 404. tech.olacabs.com/feed and bytes.swiggy.com/feed fail to connect. blog.razorpay.com/feed/ served 200 with 10 items on first contact, then refused TCP connections entirely (SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL, then connection refused) on every later attempt — it appears to block an IP after a few fetches. Removed rather than shipped as a source that fails every run.
$mediumNotes.ciVsLocal: IMPORTANT and counter-intuitive: Medium-family feeds are MORE reliable from GitHub Actions than from a laptop. After a burst of local testing, every Medium domain (medium.com tag feeds, itnext.io, levelup.gitconnected.com, blog.hotstar.com, eng.lyft.com) returned 429 "Just a moment..." from this residential IP, while the same feeds all returned green from the Actions runner minutes later. So do not delete a Medium feed because it fails locally — check data/status.json from the last CI run first.

reddit.$comment: ONE request per run, rotating by UTC hour. Measured 2026-07-29: /r/<sub>/.rss returns 200, but /r/<sub>/top.json returns 403, so no upvote score is available and posts cannot be score-filtered. The first .rss request succeeds and every subsequent one returns 429 even at 3s spacing — the limit is per-IP and unforgiving. Fetching the whole list in one run would mean one success and seven refusals, so we rotate instead and let coverage accumulate across the day's runs.
reddit.$ifYouWantItReliable: Register a free Reddit 'script' app for OAuth (100 queries/min). That needs a client id and secret, which would have to be added as GitHub repository secrets — not done here, since it is credential handling the owner should do himself if he wants it.

hackerNews.$comment: Algolia's HN Search API is public and key-free, and returns points/comments in one request — unlike the official Firebase API, which needs 1+N calls for 500 story ids. news.ycombinator.com/robots.txt sets Crawl-delay: 30 and does not disallow feeds; one request per run is well within that.
hackerNews.$trap: Use tags=front_page, NOT tags=story. With no `query` param the /search endpoint ranks by all-time popularity, so tags=story returns 2016-2024 classics ('Stephen Hawking has died', the xz backdoor) with HTTP 200 and healthy-looking item counts. They then vanish at the retention filter, so the collector reports 25 items and the dashboard shows zero.

devTo.$comment: Public, no key. The list endpoint returns description only. top=7 asks for the week's best per tag, which filters out most low-effort posts; minReactions trims further. Tags chosen for senior-level topics rather than breadth.

github.$comment: Unauthenticated GitHub Search API allows 10 req/min PER IP — and on a shared/NAT address the separate `core` bucket (60/hr) is often already exhausted by others, so we only use `search`, which embeds the license object for free. In CI, always pass the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN (30 search req/min). The REST search API does NOT support boolean OR between qualifiers — it returns HTTP 422 — so use one topic per query.
